## Introduction / 引言
===Original===

In giving the general title of “The Human Comedy” to a work begun nearly thirteen years since, it is necessary to explain its motive, to relate its origin, and briefly sketch its plan, while endeavoring to speak of these matters as though I had no personal interest in them. This is not so difficult as the public might imagine. Few works conduce to much vanity; much labor conduces to great diffidence. This observation accounts for the study of their own works made by Corneille, Molière, and other great writers; if it is impossible to equal them in their fine conceptions, we may try to imitate them in this feeling.
The idea of The Human Comedy was at first as a dream to me, one of those impossible projects which we caress and then let fly; a chimera that gives us a glimpse of its smiling woman’s face, and forthwith spreads its wings and returns to a heavenly realm of fantasy. But this chimera, like many another, has become a reality; has its behests, its tyranny, which must be obeyed.
The idea originated in a comparison between Humanity and Animality.
It is a mistake to suppose that the great dispute which has lately made a stir, between Cuvier and Geoffroi Saint-Hilaire, arose from a scientific innovation. Unity of structure, under other names, had occupied the greatest minds during the two previous centuries. As we read the extraordinary writings of the mystics who studied the sciences in their relation to infinity, such as Swedenborg, Saint-Martin, and others, and the works of the greatest authors on Natural History﻿—Leibnitz, Buffon, Charles Bonnet, etc., we detect in the *monads* of Leibnitz, in the *organic molecules* of Buffon, in the *vegetative force* of Needham, in the correlation of similar organs of Charles Bonnet﻿—who in 1760 was so bold as to write, “Animals vegetate as plants do”﻿—we detect, I say, the rudiments of the great law of Self for Self, which lies at the root of *Unity of Plan*. There is but one Animal. The Creator works on a single model for every organized being. “The Animal” is elementary, and takes its external form, or, to be accurate, the differences in its form, from the environment in which it is obliged to develop. Zoological species are the result of these differences.

===Chinese===

将「人间喜剧」这个总标题赋予一部将近十三年前动笔的作品，就有必要说明其动机、叙述其缘起，并简略勾勒其规划，同时尽力以仿佛事不关己的口吻来谈论这些事情。这并不像公众想象的那么难。很少有作品能助长多少虚荣；大量的劳作却只会带来巨大的惶恐不安。这一观察可以解释高乃依、莫里哀以及其他伟大作家为何要研究自己的作品；即便我们无法在精妙的构思上与他们比肩，也可以在这种心境上效法他们。
「人间喜剧」的构想起初于我不过是一场梦，是那种我们姑且珍惜、随即又任其飞走的不可能实现的计划；是一头奇美拉，让我们瞥见它那张含笑的女子面容，随即又振翅飞回幻想的天国。但这头奇美拉，和许多别的一样，竟成了现实；它有它的号令，它的专横，不容不从。
这个念头源于对人性与兽性的比较。
若以为居维叶与若弗鲁瓦·圣伊莱尔之间那场近来闹得沸沸扬扬的大论战起于某项科学创新，那就错了。「结构统一」换了别的名目，在此前两个世纪里早已占据过最伟大的头脑。当我们读那些把诸门科学放在与无限的关系中加以研究的神秘主义者的惊世之作——如斯威登堡、圣马丁等人——以及最伟大的博物学作家的著作——莱布尼茨、布封、夏尔·博内等，我们在莱布尼茨的「单子」里、在布封的「有机分子」里、在尼达姆的「生长力」里、在夏尔·博内的同类器官相关说里——他早在1760年便胆敢写道：「动物像植物一样营植物性生活」——我说，我们在其中察见了「自为」这条伟大法则的萌芽，而它正是「统一蓝图」的根基。动物只有一个。造物主以同一个模子造出一切有机生物。「动物」是要素性的，它被迫在其中发育的环境，决定了它的外形，或者确切地说，决定了它形态上的种种差异。动物学的种，便是这些差异的结果。

===Original===

The announcement and defence of this system, which is indeed in harmony with our preconceived ideas of Divine Power, will be the eternal glory of Geoffroi Saint-Hilaire, Cuvier’s victorious opponent on this point of higher science, whose triumph was hailed by Goethe in the last article he wrote.
I, for my part, convinced of this scheme of nature long before the discussion to which it has given rise, perceived that in this respect society resembled nature. For does not society modify Man, according to the conditions in which he lives and acts, into men as manifold as the species in Zoology? The differences between a soldier, an artisan, a man of business, a lawyer, an idler, a student, a statesman, a merchant, a sailor, a poet, a beggar, a priest, are as great, though not so easy to define, as those between the wolf, the lion, the ass, the crow, the shark, the seal, the sheep, etc. Thus social species have always existed, and will always exist, just as there are zoological species. If Buffon could produce a magnificent work by attempting to represent in a book the whole realm of zoology, was there not room for a work of the same kind on society? But the limits set by nature to the variations of animals have no existence in society. When Buffon describes the lion, he dismisses the lioness with a few phrases; but in society a wife is not always the female of the male. There may be two perfectly dissimilar beings in one household. The wife of a shopkeeper is sometimes worthy of a prince, and the wife of a prince is often worthless compared with the wife of an artisan. The social state has freaks which Nature does not allow herself; it is nature *plus* society. The description of social species would thus be at least double that of animal species, merely in view of the two sexes. Then, among animals the drama is limited; there is scarcely any confusion; they turn and rend each other﻿—that is all. Men, too, rend each other; but their greater or less intelligence makes the struggle far more complicated. Though some savants do not yet admit that the animal nature flows into human nature through an immense tide of life, the grocer certainly becomes a peer, and the noble sometimes sinks to the lowest social grade. Again, Buffon found that life was extremely simple among animals.

===Chinese===

宣布并捍卫这一体系——它确实与我们关于神力的先入之见相合——将是若弗鲁瓦·圣伊莱尔永恒的光荣；在这门高等科学的这一点上，他是居维叶的胜利者，他的凯旋得到了歌德绝笔文章的礼赞。
至于我，早在这场争论兴起之前便已信服自然的这一方案，并且看出社会在这方面正类似自然。社会岂不是按照人生活与活动的条件，把「人」改造成如同动物学中诸物种一般形形色色的「人们」吗？士兵、工匠、商人、律师、闲汉、学生、政治家、买卖人、水手、诗人、乞丐、教士，他们之间的差异，虽然不那么容易界定，却同狼、狮、驴、鸦、鲨、海豹、羊之间的差异一样大。可见社会物种向来存在，并将永远存在，正如动物学物种一样。既然布封试图在一部书里再现整个动物学界而写出了煌煌巨著，那么为社会写一部同类著作，岂非也有其一席之地？只是自然为动物变异所设的界限，在社会中并不存在。布封描写狮子时，几笔便打发了母狮；而在社会里，妻子并不总是雄性的雌性对应。一个家庭里可能有两个截然不同的存在。小店主的妻子有时配得上一位亲王，而亲王的妻子比起工匠的妻子来又往往一文不值。社会状态有着自然不敢放纵自己的种种任性；它是自然「加」社会。仅就两性而论，对社会物种的描写便至少要比动物物种多出一倍。再说，动物之间的戏剧是有限的；几乎没有什么错综纠葛；它们相互撕咬——如此而已。人也互相撕咬；但智力的高下使这场斗争复杂得多。尽管有些学者还不承认动物本性经由一条浩瀚的生命之流汇入人性，杂货商确乎能当上贵族院议员，而贵族有时会沦落到社会的最底层。再者，布封发现动物的生活极其简单。

===Original===

Animals have little property, and neither arts nor sciences; while man, by a law that has yet to be sought, has a tendency to express his culture, his thoughts, and his life in everything he appropriates to his use. Though Leuwenhoek, Swammerdam, Spallanzani, Réaumur, Charles Bonnet, Müller, Haller and other patient investigators have shown us how interesting are the habits of animals, those of each kind, are, at least to our eyes, always and in every age alike; whereas the dress, the manners, the speech, the dwelling of a prince, a banker, an artist, a citizen, a priest, and a pauper are absolutely unlike, and change with every phase of civilization.
Hence the work to be written needed a threefold form﻿—men, women, and things; that is to say, persons and the material expression of their minds; man, in short, and life.
As we read the dry and discouraging list of events called History, who can have failed to note that the writers of all periods, in Egypt, Persia, Greece, and Rome, have forgotten to give us a history of manners? The fragment of Petronius on the private life of the Romans excites rather than satisfies our curiosity. It was from observing this great void in the field of history that the Abbé Barthélemy devoted his life to a reconstruction of Greek manners in *Le Jeune Anacharsis*.
But how could such a drama, with the four or five thousand persons which society offers, be made interesting? How, at the same time, please the poet, the philosopher, and the masses who want both poetry and philosophy under striking imagery? Though I could conceive of the importance and of the poetry of such a history of the human heart, I saw no way of writing it; for hitherto the most famous storytellers had spent their talent in creating two or three typical actors, in depicting one aspect of life. It was with this idea that I read the works of Walter Scott. Walter Scott, the modern troubadour, or finder (*trouvère*=*trouveur*), had just then given an aspect of grandeur to a class of composition unjustly regarded as of the second rank.

===Chinese===

动物几乎没有财产，也没有艺术和科学；而人，依照一条尚待探究的法则，倾向于在一切为他所用的东西上打上他的教养、思想和生活的印记。尽管列文虎克、斯瓦默丹、斯帕兰扎尼、列奥米尔、夏尔·博内、缪勒、哈勒等耐心的研究者已让我们看到动物的习性何等有趣，但每一类动物的习性，至少在我们眼里，古今如一、处处相同；而亲王、银行家、艺术家、市民、教士和贫民的衣着、举止、谈吐、居所却截然不同，并且随文明的每一阶段而变。
因此，要写的这部作品需要一种三重形式——男人、女人和事物；也就是说，人物以及他们心灵的外在表现；简言之，人及其生活。
读着那部名为历史的枯燥而令人气馁的事件编目，谁能不注意到，历代的一切著述家，无论在埃及、波斯、希腊还是罗马，都忘了给我们留下一部风俗史？佩特罗尼乌斯写罗马人私生活的那部残卷，只会撩起而不能满足我们的好奇心。正是有感于历史领域的这一巨大空白，巴泰勒米神甫才以毕生精力在《小阿纳卡尔西斯的希腊之旅》（*Le Jeune Anacharsis*）中重构希腊风俗。
可是，这样一出由社会提供的四五千个人物组成的戏剧，怎样才能写得引人入胜？又怎样才能同时取悦诗人、哲学家，以及那班要求诗意与哲思都裹着醒目形象的民众？我虽能体会到这样一部人类心灵史的重要与诗意，却看不出如何落笔；因为迄今为止，最有名的说故事的人都把才华用在塑造两三个典型人物、描绘生活的一个侧面上。正是带着这个念头，我读了瓦尔特·司各特的作品。瓦尔特·司各特，这位现代的行吟诗人，或者说「发现者」（trouvère=trouveur），彼时刚为一类素来被不公正地目为二流的写作赋予了庄严的气象。

===Original===

Is it not really more difficult to compete with personal and parochial interests by writing of Daphnis and Chloe, Roland, Amadis, Panurge, Don Quixote, Manon Lescaut, Clarissa, Lovelace, Robinson Crusoe, Gil Blas, Ossian, Julie d’Etanges, My Uncle Toby, Werther, Corinne, Adolphe, Paul and Virginia, Jeanie Deans, Claverhouse, Ivanhoe, Manfred, Mignon, than to set forth in order facts more or less similar in every country, to investigate the spirit of laws that have fallen into desuetude, to review the theories which mislead nations, or, like some metaphysicians, to explain what *Is*? In the first place, these actors, whose existence becomes more prolonged and more authentic than that of the generations which saw their birth, almost always live solely on condition of their being a vast reflection of the present. Conceived in the womb of their own period, the whole heart of humanity stirs within their frame, which often covers a complete system of philosophy. Thus Walter Scott raised to the dignity of the philosophy of History the literature which, from age to age, sets perennial gems in the poetic crown of every nation where letters are cultivated. He vivified it with the spirit of the past; he combined drama, dialogue, portrait, scenery, and description; he fused the marvelous with truth﻿—the two elements of the times; and he brought poetry into close contact with the familiarity of the humblest speech. But as he had not so much devised a system as hit upon a manner in the ardor of his work, or as its logical outcome, he never thought of connecting his compositions in such a way as to form a complete history of which each chapter was a novel, and each novel the picture of a period.
It was by discerning this lack of unity, which in no way detracts from the Scottish writer’s greatness, that I perceived at once the scheme which would favor the execution of my purpose, and the possibility of executing it. Though dazzled, so to speak, by Walter Scott’s amazing fertility, always himself and always original, I did not despair, for I found the source of his genius in the infinite variety of human nature. Chance is the greatest romancer in the world; we have only to study it. French society would be the real author; I should only be the secretary.

===Chinese===

写下达佛涅斯和克洛伊、罗兰、阿马迪斯、巴汝奇、堂吉诃德、曼侬·莱斯科、克拉丽莎、洛夫莱斯、鲁滨逊·克鲁索、吉尔·布拉斯、莪相、于丽·代当热、我的托比叔叔、维特、柯丽娜、阿道尔夫、保罗与弗吉尼亚、珍妮·迪恩斯、克莱弗豪斯、艾凡赫、曼弗雷德、迷娘，以此与个人利益和地方利益相抗衡——这难道不真的比罗列各国大同小异的事实、探究已废止法律的法理、检讨那些误导民族的理论，或像某些形而上学家那样去解释「存在」更难吗？首先，这些人物的寿命比目睹他们诞生的世代更长久、更真切，而他们之所以能存在，几乎全凭成为当下时代的一幅广阔映照。他们孕育于自己时代的子宫，人类的整颗心在他们的躯壳里跳动，那躯壳往往包裹着一整套哲学体系。瓦尔特·司各特就是这样把那种代代相传、在凡有文学之邦的诗之冠冕上镶嵌不朽宝石的写作，提升到了历史哲学的尊严。他以往昔的精神使它鲜活；他把戏剧、对话、肖像、风景和描写熔于一炉；他把神奇与真实——时代的两大元素——冶于一处；他让诗歌与最卑下言谈的家常亲切紧紧相贴。但他与其说是创立了一个体系，不如说是在创作的热忱中、在创作的逻辑结局里碰上了一种写法，因此他从未想过把他的各部作品联结起来，构成一部完整的历史，其中每章是一部小说，每部小说是一个时代的画卷。
正是辨出了这种统一性的缺失——它丝毫无损于这位苏格兰作家的伟大——我顿时看清了有利于实现我的目标的方案，以及实现它的可能。尽管可以说被瓦尔特·司各特那始终如一、永远独创的惊人才思照得目眩，我却不曾绝望，因为我在人性的无穷多样中找到了他天才的源头。机缘是世界上最伟大的小说家；我们只需研究它。法兰西社会将是真正的作者；我不过是它的书记。

===Original===

By drawing up an inventory of vices and virtues, by collecting the chief facts of the passions, by depicting characters, by choosing the principal incidents of social life, by composing types out of a combination of homogeneous characteristics, I might perhaps succeed in writing the history which so many historians have neglected: that of Manners. By patience and perseverance I might produce for France in the nineteenth century the book which we must all regret that Rome, Athens, Tyre, Memphis, Persia, and India have not bequeathed to us; that history of their social life which, prompted by the Abbé Barthélemy, Monteil patiently and steadily tried to write for the Middle Ages, but in an unattractive form.
This work, so far, was nothing. By adhering to the strict lines of a reproduction a writer might be a more or less faithful, and more or less successful, painter of types of humanity, a narrator of the dramas of private life, an archaeologist of social furniture, a cataloguer of professions, a registrar of good and evil; but to deserve the praise of which every artist must be ambitious, must I not also investigate the reasons or the cause of these social effects, detect the hidden sense of this vast assembly of figures, passions, and incidents? And finally, having sought﻿—I will not say having found﻿—this reason, this motive power, must I not reflect on first principles, and discover in what particulars societies approach or deviate from the eternal law of truth and beauty? In spite of the wide scope of the preliminaries, which might of themselves constitute a book, the work, to be complete, would need a conclusion. Thus depicted, society ought to bear in itself the reason of its working.
The law of the writer, in virtue of which he is a writer, and which I do not hesitate to say makes him the equal, or perhaps the superior, of the statesman, is his judgment, whatever it may be, on human affairs, and his absolute devotion to certain principles. Machiavelli, Hobbes, Bossuet, Leibnitz, Kant, Montesquieu, *are* the science which statesmen apply. “A writer ought to have settled opinions on morals and politics; he should regard himself as a tutor of men; for men need no masters to teach them to doubt,” says Bonald. I took these noble words as my guide long ago; they are the written law of the monarchical writer.

===Chinese===

编制一份善恶的清单，搜集群情感的主要事实，刻画性格，选取社会生活的主要事变，把同类的特征糅合起来塑成典型，我或许便能写出那部被众多史家忽略了的历史：风俗史。凭着耐心与毅力，我或许能为十九世纪的法兰西写出一部书——一部我们人人都该惋惜罗马、雅典、推罗、孟菲斯、波斯和印度不曾传给我们的书；巴泰勒米神甫的启发促使蒙泰伊为中世纪耐心而坚定地试写过那样的社会生活史，只是形式缺乏吸引力。
到此为止，这番事业还不算什么。倘若拘守于如实复刻的严格界限，一个作家充其量是或忠或不忠、或成或不成的人类典型画师，私生活戏剧的讲述者，社会陈设的考古家，职业的编目人，善恶的登记员；但要博得每个艺术家都当渴求的赞誉，我不还得去探究这些社会效果的缘由或成因，去参透这一大群人物、情感与事变集合的隐义吗？而最终，在寻得了——我不说找到了——这个缘由、这个动力之后，我不还得对第一原理加以思索，查明社会在哪些方面接近、又偏离了真与美的永恒法则吗？尽管这些绪论本身便足以构成一部书、范围如此之广，但作品要完整，还需要一个结论。这样描绘出来的社会，理应自身携带着它运行的缘由。
作家的法则，即他之所以为作家的那条法则——我毫不犹豫地说，它使作家与政治家平起平坐，甚至或许犹有过之——就是他对人事的评判，无论那评判如何，以及他对某些原则的绝对忠诚。马基雅维利、霍布斯、博叙埃、莱布尼茨、康德、孟德斯鸠，「就是」政治家们所运用的那门科学。「作家对道德与政治应有定见；他应当自视为世人的导师；因为世人无需谁来教他们怀疑。」博纳尔如是说。我早已把这些高贵的话奉为圭臬；它们是君主派作家的成文法。

===Original===

And those who would confute me by my own words will find that they have misinterpreted some ironical phrase, or that they have turned against me a speech given to one of my actors﻿—a trick peculiar to calumniators.
As to the intimate purpose, the soul of this work, these are the principles on which it is based.
Man is neither good nor bad; he is born with instincts and capabilities; society, far from depraving him, as Rousseau asserts, improves him, makes him better; but self-interest also develops his evil tendencies. Christianity, above all, Catholicism, being﻿—as I have pointed out in the Country Doctor (*le Médecin de Campagne*)﻿—a complete system for the repression of the depraved tendencies of man, is the most powerful element of social order.
In reading attentively the presentment of society cast, as it were, from the life, with all that is good and all that is bad in it, we learn this lesson﻿—if thought, or if passion, which combines thought and feeling, is the vital social element, it is also its destructive element. In this respect social life is like the life of man. Nations live long only by moderating their vital energy. Teaching, or rather education, by religious bodies is the grand principle of life for nations, the only means of diminishing the sum of evil and increasing the sum of good in all society. Thought, the living principle of good and ill, can only be trained, quelled, and guided by religion. The only possible religion is Christianity (see the letter from Paris in “Louis Lambert,” in which the young mystic explains, apropos to Swedenborg’s doctrines, how there has never been but one religion since the world began). Christianity created modern nationalities, and it will preserve them. Hence, no doubt, the necessity for the monarchical principle. Catholicism and Royalty are twin principles.
As to the limits within which these two principles should be confined by various institutions, so that they may not become absolute, everyone will feel that a brief preface ought not to be a political treatise. I cannot, therefore, enter on religious discussions, nor on the political discussions of the day. I write under the light of two eternal truths﻿—Religion and Monarchy; two necessities, as they are shown to be by contemporary events, towards which every writer of sound sense ought to try to guide the country back.

===Chinese===

至于那些想引用我自己的话来驳我的人，他们终会发现，自己要么误解了某句反语，要么把我笔下人物的台词栽到我头上——这是诽谤者的惯技。
至于这部作品深藏的用意、它的灵魂，其立足的原则如下。
人无所谓善，也无所谓恶；他与生俱来的是本能与禀赋；社会远不像卢梭断言的那样使人败坏，而是改善人、使人向善；但私利也会发展人作恶的倾向。基督教，尤其是天主教——如我在《乡村医生》（*le Médecin de Campagne*）中指出的——是一套遏制人性堕落倾向的完整体系，是社会秩序最强大的要素。
细读这幅宛如从生活中翻铸出来的社会图景，连同其中一切的善与一切的恶，我们会得到这样的教训——思想，或者说情感（它兼含思想与感受），若是社会生命的要素，它也是社会的毁灭要素。在这方面，社会生活一如人的生活。民族唯有节制其生命活力方能长寿。由宗教团体施行的教导，毋宁说教育，是民族生命的宏大原则，是减少全社会之恶、增加全社会之善的唯一手段。思想，这善恶的活本原，唯有靠宗教才能驯服、平息和引导。唯一可能的宗教是基督教（见《路易·朗贝尔》中那封巴黎来信，年轻的神秘主义者在信中借斯威登堡的学说说明，自开天辟地以来从来只有一种宗教）。基督教创造了近代诸民族，也将保全他们。因此，君主原则之必要，当无可疑。天主教与王权是一对孪生原则。
至于这两项原则应由种种制度限制在什么范围之内才不致流于绝对，人人都会明白，一篇短短的序言不该写成政治论文。因此，我不会涉足宗教论争，也不谈当日的政治纷争。我在两条永恒真理——宗教与君主制——的光照之下写作；时事已证明它们是两种必然，每一位头脑健全的作家都应努力引导国家重返这两者。

===Original===

Without being an enemy to election, which is an excellent principle as a basis of legislation, I reject election regarded as *the only social instrument*, especially so badly organized as it now is (1842); for it fails to represent imposing minorities, whose ideas and interests would occupy the attention of a monarchical government. Elective power extended to all gives us government by the masses, the only irresponsible form of government, under which tyranny is unlimited, for it calls itself law. Besides, I regard the family and not the individual as the true social unit. In this respect, at the risk of being thought retrograde, I side with Bossuet and Bonald instead of going with modern innovators. Since election has become the only social instrument, if I myself were to exercise it no contradiction between my acts and my words should be inferred. An engineer points out that a bridge is about to fall, that it is dangerous for anyone to cross it; but he crosses it himself when it is the only road to the town. Napoleon adapted election to the spirit of the French nation with wonderful skill. The least important members of his Legislative Body became the most famous orators of the Chamber after the Restoration. No Chamber has ever been the equal of the Corps Législatif, comparing them man for man. The elective system of the Empire was, then, indisputably the best.
Some persons may, perhaps, think that this declaration is somewhat autocratic and self-assertive. They will quarrel with the novelist for wanting to be an historian, and will call him to account for writing politics. I am simply fulfilling an obligation﻿—that is my reply. The work I have undertaken will be as long as a history; I was compelled to explain the logic of it, hitherto unrevealed, and its principles and moral purpose.
Having been obliged to withdraw the prefaces formerly published, in response to essentially ephemeral criticisms, I will retain only one remark.
Writers who have a purpose in view, were it only a reversion to principles familiar in the past because they are eternal, should always clear the ground. Now everyone who, in the domain of ideas, brings his stone by pointing out an abuse, or setting a mark on some evil that it may be removed﻿—every such man is stigmatized as immoral.

===Chinese===

我并非选举之敌——作为立法的基础，它是一条极好的原则；但我拒绝把选举奉为「唯一的社会工具」，尤其当它组织得像如今（1842年）这般糟糕的时候；因为它未能代表那些可观的少数派，而他们的思想与利益本该受到君主政府的关注。把选举权扩及所有人，给我们带来的是群众的统治，那是唯一不负责任的政体，其下暴政没有限度，因为它自命为法律。此外，我认为真正的社会单位是家庭而非个人。在这一点上，我宁可被视为保守倒退，站在博叙埃和博纳尔一边，而不追随现代的革新者。既然选举已成唯一的社会工具，那么倘若我自己也去投票，也不应被推断为言行相悖。工程师指出一座桥快要塌了，谁过谁危险；但若是进城仅有此路，他自己也会从桥上走。拿破仑（Napoleon）以绝妙的技巧使选举契合法兰西民族的精神。他的立法团里最无足轻重的成员，在王政复辟（the Restoration）之后成了议院里最著名的演说家。逐人相比，历届议院没有一个比得上帝国时期的立法团。所以说，帝国的选举制度无可争辩是最好的。
也许有人觉得这番宣言未免专断自负。他们会责怪小说家想当历史学家，会追究他谈政治。我只是在履行一项义务——这就是我的回答。我着手做的这部作品将有一部历史那样长；我不得不说明它至今未曾揭示的逻辑，以及它的原则与道德目的。
既然不得不应那些本质上转瞬即逝的批评撤回先前发表的诸篇序言，这里我只想保留一句话。
有目标的作家——哪怕目标只是回到过去那些因永恒而为人熟稔的原则——总该廓清场地。而在思想的领域里，凡指摘一种弊病、或给某种恶行做上标记以便铲除而献上一己之石的——这样的人个个都被烙上不道德的印记。

===Original===

The accusation of immorality, which has never failed to be cast at the courageous writer, is, after all, the last that can be brought when nothing else remains to be said to a romancer. If you are truthful in your pictures; if by dint of daily and nightly toil you succeed in writing the most difficult language in the world, the word *immoral* is flung in your teeth. Socrates was immoral; Jesus Christ was immoral; they both were persecuted in the name of the society they overset or reformed. When a man is to be killed he is taxed with immorality. These tactics, familiar in party warfare, are a disgrace to those who use them. Luther and Calvin knew well what they were about when they shielded themselves behind damaged worldly interests! And they lived all the days of their life.
When depicting all society, sketching it in the immensity of its turmoil, it happened﻿—it could not but happen﻿—that the picture displayed more of evil than of good; that some part of the fresco represented a guilty couple; and the critics at once raised a cry of immorality, without pointing out the morality of another position intended to be a perfect contrast. As the critic knew nothing of the general plan I could forgive him, all the more because one can no more hinder criticism than the use of eyes, tongues, and judgment. Also the time for an impartial verdict is not yet come for me. And, after all, the author who cannot make up his mind to face the fire of criticism should no more think of writing than a traveler should start on his journey counting on a perpetually clear sky. On this point it remains to be said that the most conscientious moralists doubt greatly whether society can show as many good actions as bad ones; and in the picture I have painted of it there are more virtuous figures than reprehensible ones. Blameworthy actions, faults and crimes, from the lightest to the most atrocious, always meet with punishment, human or divine, signal or secret. I have done better than the historian, for I am free. Cromwell here on earth escaped all punishment but that inflicted by thoughtful men. And on this point there have been divided schools. Bossuet even showed some consideration for great regicide. William of Orange, the usurper, Hugues Capet, another usurper, lived to old age with no more qualms or fears than Henri IV or Charles I.

===Chinese===

「不道德」这项指控，从未放过任何勇敢的作家，说到底，它是对小说家无话可说时最后抛出的一顶帽子。倘若你的画面真实；倘若你靠日夜辛劳终于驾驭了世界上最难的语言，「不道德」三个字就会啐到你脸上。苏格拉底是不道德的；耶稣基督是不道德的；两人都以他们所倾覆或所改造的那个社会的名义遭受迫害。欲置一人于死地，便给他扣上不道德的罪名。这套党争中司空见惯的手法，是使用者自己的耻辱。路德和加尔文躲在被损害的世俗利益背后，他们心里雪亮自己在干什么！而他们全都活完了天年。
描绘整个社会，勾勒它纷乱的浩瀚图景时，难免——不可避免地——画面里显露的恶多于善；壁画总有某一部分画着一对罪人；批评家们便立刻大呼不道德，却不肯指出另一处立意与之恰成对照的人物身上所含的道德。既然批评家对总体规划一无所知，我可以原谅他，何况人们阻止不了批评，正如阻止不了人们用眼睛、用舌头、下判断。况且，对我作出公正裁决的时机也尚未到来。再说，打定主意受不了批评之火的作家，趁早别想写作，正如指望天空永远晴朗的旅人趁早别上路。关于这一点，还要说的是：最一丝不苟的道德家们也极怀疑社会拿得出与恶行同样多的善行；而在我画的这幅社会图景里，可敬的人物多于可责的人物。应受谴责的行为、过失与罪恶，从最轻到最重，总逃不脱或人世或上天、或昭彰或隐秘的惩罚。我比历史学家做得更好，因为我是自由的。克伦威尔在人间逃脱了一切惩罚，只除了有思想的人加于他的那一重。在这一点上历来学派纷纭。博叙埃甚至对伟大的弑君者也不无体谅。篡位的奥兰治的威廉，还有另一个篡位者于格·卡佩，都活到耄耋之年，心中无愧无惧，不亚于亨利四世或查理一世。

===Original===

The lives of Catherine II and of Frederick of Prussia would be conclusive against any kind of moral law, if they were judged by the twofold aspect of the morality which guides ordinary mortals, and that which is in use by crowned heads; for, as Napoleon said, for kings and statesmen there are the lesser and the higher morality. My scenes of political life are founded on this profound observation. It is not a law to history, as it is to romance, to make for a beautiful ideal. History is, or ought to be, what it was; while romance ought to be “the better world,” as was said by Mme. Necker, one of the most distinguished thinkers of the last century.
Still, with this noble falsity, romance would be nothing if it were not true in detail. Walter Scott, obliged as he was to conform to the ideas of an essentially hypocritical nation, was false to humanity in his picture of woman, because his models were schismatics. The Protestant woman has no ideal. She may be chaste, pure, virtuous; but her unexpansive love will always be as calm and methodical as the fulfilment of a duty. It might seem as though the Virgin Mary had chilled the hearts of those sophists who have banished her from heaven with her treasures of loving kindness. In Protestantism there is no possible future for the woman who has sinned; while, in the Catholic Church, the hope of forgiveness makes her sublime. Hence, for the Protestant writer there is but one Woman, while the Catholic writer finds a new woman in each new situation. If Walter Scott had been a Catholic, if he had set himself the task of describing truly the various phases of society which have successively existed in Scotland, perhaps the painter of Effie and Alice﻿—the two figures for which he blamed himself in his later years﻿—might have admitted passion with its sins and punishments, and the virtues revealed by repentance. Passion is the sum-total of humanity. Without passion, religion, history, romance, art, would all be useless.
Some persons, seeing me collect such a mass of facts and paint them as they are, with passion for their motive power, have supposed, but wrongly, that I must belong to the school of Sensualism and Materialism﻿—two aspects of the same thing﻿—Pantheism. But their misapprehension was perhaps justified﻿—or inevitable.

===Chinese===

叶卡捷琳娜二世和普鲁士的腓特烈的生平，倘若按凡人遵行的道德与戴王冠者通行的道德这双重视角来评判，便可断定一切道德律皆属子虚；因为正如拿破仑所说，为君者与政治家有低级道德与高级道德之分。我的政治生活场景便建立在这条深刻的观察之上。历史不同于小说，不以求取美好的理想为法则。历史是或应当是已然之事；而小说应当是「更好的世界」，上个世纪最杰出的思想家之一内克尔夫人如是说。
然而，怀着这份高贵的失真，小说若在细节上不真实，便一文不值。瓦尔特·司各特迫于迁就一个骨子里伪善的民族的意见，在女性画像上背离了人性，因为他的原型都是异端之徒。新教徒妇女没有理想。她可以贞洁、纯净、有德；但她那不曾舒展的爱，永远像履行义务一般平静而有条不紊。仿佛圣母玛利亚寒透了那些诡辩家的心，他们把她连同她满怀慈爱的宝藏一起逐出了天国。在新教里，失足的女子没有任何前途；而在天主教会中，宽恕的希望使她崇高。因此，新教作家笔下只有唯一的「女人」，而天主教作家则在每个新情境中都能发现一个新的女人。倘若瓦尔特·司各特是天主教徒，倘若他给自己定下如实地描写苏格兰历代社会各阶段的任务，那么埃菲和艾丽斯的画师——他晚年曾为这两个人物自责——或许就会容纳连同其罪孽与惩罚在内的激情，以及由悔悟而显明的美德了。激情是人性的总和。没有激情，宗教、历史、小说、艺术，都将毫无用处。
有些人见我搜罗如许大量的事实，并以激情为其动力如实描绘，便想当然地——却想错了——认定我必属感官主义与唯物主义学派——二者本是同一回事的两个方面——即泛神论。但他们的误解或许情有可原——或者说在所难免。

===Original===

I do not share the belief in indefinite progress for society as a whole; I believe in man’s improvement in himself. Those who insist on reading in me the intention to consider man as a finished creation are strangely mistaken. *Séraphita*, the doctrine in action of the Christian Buddha, seems to me an ample answer to this rather heedless accusation.
In certain fragments of this long work I have tried to popularize the amazing facts, I may say the marvels, of electricity, which in man is metamorphosed into an incalculable force; but in what way do the phenomena of brain and nerves, which prove the existence of an undiscovered world of psychology, modify the necessary and undoubted relations of the worlds to God? In what way can they shake the Catholic dogma? Though irrefutable facts should some day place thought in the class of fluids which are discerned only by their effects while their substance evades our senses, even when aided by so many mechanical means, the result will be the same as when Christopher Columbus detected that the earth is a sphere, and Galileo demonstrated its rotation. Our future will be unchanged. The wonders of animal magnetism, with which I have been familiar since 1820; the beautiful experiments of Gall, Lavater’s successor; all the men who have studied mind as opticians have studied light﻿—two not dissimilar things﻿—point to a conclusion in favor of the mystics, the disciples of St. John, and of those great thinkers who have established the spiritual world﻿—the sphere in which are revealed the relations of God and man.
A sure grasp of the purport of this work will make it clear that I attach to common, daily facts, hidden or patent to the eye, to the acts of individual lives, and to their causes and principles, the importance which historians have hitherto ascribed to the events of public national life. The unknown struggle which goes on in a valley of the Indre between Mme. de Mortsauf and her passion is perhaps as great as the most famous of battles (*Le Lys dans la Valleé*). In one the glory of the victor is at stake; in the other it is heaven. The misfortunes of the two Birotteaus, the priest and the perfumer, to me are those of mankind. La Fosseuse (*Médecin de Campagne*) and Mme. Graslin (*Curé de Village*) are almost the sum-total of woman. We all suffer thus every day.

===Chinese===

我不相信社会整体有无限的进步；我相信的是人自身的完善。硬要从我这里读出「把人看作已然完成的造物」这种意图的人，实在错得离谱。《塞拉菲塔》，这位基督佛陀的学说之现身说法，在我看来足可回敬这颇为轻率的指控。
在这部长篇巨帙的某些片段里，我试图使电的那些惊人事迹——不妨说是奇迹——广为人知；电在人身上转化为一种不可估量的力量；可是，大脑与神经的现象纵然证明了心理学中一个尚未发现的世界，它们又怎能改变诸世界与上帝之间必然而确凿的关系？它们又怎能动摇天主教的教义？即使有朝一日无可辩驳的事实把思想归入流体一类——只能凭效应察觉而其实体逃脱我们感官的流体，纵然借助如此之多的机械手段——其结果也不过如克里斯托弗·哥伦布发现大地是球形、伽利略证明地球自转一样。我们的未来不会因此改变。动物磁流的种种奇观，我自1820年起便已熟稔；加尔——拉瓦特的继承者——的那些美妙实验；所有像光学研究者研究光那样研究心灵的人——这两样东西并非不相似——都指向一个有利于神秘主义者、圣约翰的门徒、以及那些确立了精神世界——上帝与人的关系在其中得以启示的领域——的伟大思想家的结论。
切实把握了这部作品的主旨，便会明白：我赋予日常的、或隐或显的普通事实，赋予个人生活的行为及其动因与原则的重要性，正是史家们迄今只肯赋予民族公共生活事件的。在安德尔河（Indre）的河谷里，德·莫尔索夫人与她的激情之间进行的那场无人知晓的斗争，或许不亚于最著名的战役（《幽谷百合》）。在战场上，胜负关乎胜利者的荣耀；在那河谷里，关乎的却是天国。两个比罗托——教士和香水商——的不幸，在我眼里就是人类的不幸。拉福瑟兹（《乡村医生》）和格拉兰夫人（《乡村教士》）几乎就是女性的全部总和。我们每个人天天都在如此受苦。

===Original===

I have had to do a hundred times what Richardson did but once. Lovelace has a thousand forms, for social corruption takes the hues of the medium in which it lives. Clarissa, on the contrary, the lovely image of impassioned virtue, is drawn in lines of distracting purity. To create a variety of Virgins it needs a Raphael. In this respect, perhaps literature must yield to painting.
Still, I may be allowed to point out how many irreproachable figures﻿—as regards their virtue﻿—are to be found in the portions of this work already published: Pierrette Lorrain, Ursule Mirouêt, Constance Birotteau, La Fosseuse, Eugénie Grandet, Marguerite Claês, Pauline de Villenoix, Madame Jules, Madame de la Chanterie, Eve Chardon, Mademoiselle d’Esgrignon, Madame Firmiani, Agathe Rouget, Renée de Maucombe; besides several figures in the middle-distance, who, though less conspicuous than these, nevertheless, offer the reader an example of domestic virtue: Joseph Lebas, Genestas, Benassis, Bonnet the curé, Minoret the doctor, Pillerault, David Séchard, the two Birotteaus, Chaperon the priest, Judge Popinot, Bourgeat, the Sauviats, the Tascherons, and many more. Do not all these solve the difficult literary problem which consists in making a virtuous person interesting?
It was no small task to depict the two or three thousand conspicuous types of a period; for this is, in fact, the number presented to us by each generation, and which the Human Comedy will require. This crowd of actors, of characters, this multitude of lives, needed a setting﻿—if I may be pardoned the expression, a gallery. Hence the very natural division, as already known, into the Scenes of Private Life, of Provincial Life, of Parisian, Political, Military, and Country Life. Under these six heads are classified all the studies of manners which form the history of society at large, of all its *faits et gestes*, as our ancestors would have said. These six classes correspond, indeed, to familiar conceptions. Each has its own sense and meaning, and answers to an epoch in the life of man. I may repeat here, but very briefly, what was written by Felix Davin﻿—a young genius snatched from literature by an early death.

===Chinese===

理查逊只做过一次的事，我却不得不做上一百次。洛夫莱斯有一千种面目，因为社会腐败总是沾染上它所处环境的色调。相反，克拉丽莎，那激越美德的动人形象，是以令人心旌摇曳的纯净笔致勾画的。要画出千姿百态的圣母，须有拉斐尔。在这一层上，文学或许不得不向绘画甘拜下风。
不过，请容我指出，在这部作品已出版的部分里，就美德而论无可指摘的人物何其多：皮埃雷特·洛兰、于絮尔·弥罗埃、康斯坦斯·比罗托、拉福瑟兹、欧也妮·葛朗台、玛格丽特·克莱斯、波利娜·德·维勒努瓦、朱尔太太、德·拉·尚特里夫人、夏娃·夏尔东、德·埃斯格里尼翁小姐、费尔米安尼夫人（Madame Firmiani）、阿加特·鲁热、勒妮·德·莫孔伯；此外还有中景里的若干人物，虽不及上述诸人醒目，却同样向读者展示着家庭美德的楷模：约瑟夫·勒巴、热内斯塔、贝纳西、本堂神甫博内、医生米诺雷、皮耶罗、达维德·塞夏尔、两个比罗托、教士夏佩龙、法官波皮诺、布尔雅、索维亚一家、塔谢隆一家，等等，不一而足。所有这些人物，不都解决了「把有德之人写得引人入胜」这个文学难题吗？
描绘一个时代两三千个显要典型，绝非小工程；因为每一代人所呈献给我们的，事实上正是这个数目，而「人间喜剧」所需要的也正是这个数目。这一大群演员、这一大堆性格、这芸芸众生，需要一个布景——请原谅我这么说，一条画廊。于是便有了众所周知的那非常自然的划分：私人生活场景、外省生活场景、巴黎生活场景、政治生活场景、军事生活场景和乡村生活场景。凡构成整个社会史、用我们祖先的话说，社会的一切「行止事迹」（faits et gestes）的风俗研究，都归在这六个题目之下。这六个类别确实对应着人们熟悉的概念。每一类自有其意谓，对应着人生的一个时期。这里我可以极简略地重述费利克斯·达万写下的话——一位被早夭从文学界夺走的年轻天才。

===Original===

After being informed of my plan, he said that the Scenes of Private Life represented childhood and youth and their errors, as the Scenes of Provincial Life represented the age of passion, scheming, self-interest, and ambition. Then the Scenes of Parisian Life give a picture of the tastes and vice and unbridled powers which conduce to the habits peculiar to great cities, where the extremes of good and evil meet. Each of these divisions has its local color﻿—Paris and the Provinces﻿—a great social antithesis which held for me immense resources.
And not man alone, but the principal events of life, fall into classes by types. There are situations which occur in every life, typical phases, and this is one of the details I most sought after. I have tried to give an idea of the different districts of our fine country. My work has its geography, as it has its genealogy and its families, its places and things, its persons and their deeds; as it has its heraldry, its nobles and commonalty, its artisans and peasants, its politicians and dandies, its army﻿—in short, a whole world of its own.
After describing social life in these three portions, I had to delineate certain exceptional lives, which comprehend the interests of many people, or of everybody, and are in a degree outside the general law. Hence we have Scenes of Political Life. This vast picture of society being finished and complete, was it not needful to display it in its most violent phase, beside itself, as it were, either in self-defence or for the sake of conquest? Hence the Scenes of Military Life, as yet the most incomplete portion of my work, but for which room will be allowed in this edition, that it may form part of it when done. Finally, the Scenes of Country Life are, in a way, the evening of this long day, if I may so call the social drama. In that part are to be found the purest natures, and the application of the great principles of order, politics, and morality.

===Chinese===

他得知我的计划后说，私人生活场景写的是童年、青年及其过失，正如外省生活场景写的是激情、算计、私利与野心的年代。而巴黎生活场景则描绘了导向大都市特有习气的趣味、恶习和不受约束的权势，在那里善与恶的两极相遇。这几个部分各有其地方色彩——巴黎（Paris）与外省——这一重大的社会对照，于我是取之不尽的宝藏。
不仅人，连人生的主要事件也按类型分门别类。有些境遇人人在一生中都会经历，典型的阶段，而这正是我最着意经营的细节之一。我努力让人对我们这个美丽国家的不同地区有所认识。我的作品自有其地理，正如它自有其谱系与家族、场所与事物、人物及其事迹；正如它自有其纹章学、贵族与平民、工匠与农夫、政客与纨绔、它的军队——总之，自成一个完整的世界。
在这三个部分里描写了社会生活之后，我还得刻画某些特出的生命，它们牵涉许多人的乃至所有人的利害，在某种程度上逸出一般法则。于是有了政治生活场景。社会这幅巨画画成完备之后，岂不是还需要展示它最暴烈的一幕、可以说是忘乎所以的一幕——或为自卫，或为征服？于是有了军事生活场景，那是我作品中迄今最不完备的部分，但本版将为它留出位置，待写成后即可补入其中。最后，乡村生活场景，可以说，是这漫长一日——请容我这样称呼这出社会剧——的黄昏。在那部分里可以找到最纯洁的天性，以及秩序、政治与道德诸伟大原则的运用。

===Original===

Such is the foundation, full of actors, full of comedies and tragedies, on which are raised the Philosophical Studies﻿—the second part of my work, in which the social instrument of all these effects is displayed, and the ravages of the mind are painted, feeling after feeling; the first of the series, *The Magic Skin*, to some extent forms a link between the Philosophical Studies and Studies of Manners, by a work of almost Oriental fancy, in which life itself is shown in a mortal struggle with the very element of all passion.
Besides these, there will be a series of Analytical Studies, of which I will say nothing, for one only is published as yet﻿—The Physiology of Marriage.
In the course of time I purpose writing two more works of this class. First the Pathology of Social Life, then an Anatomy of Educational Bodies, and a Monograph on Virtue.
In looking forward to what remains to be done, my readers will perhaps echo what my publishers say, “Please God to spare you!” I only ask to be less tormented by men and things than I have hitherto been since I began this terrific labor. I have had this in my favor, and I thank God for it, that the talents of the time, the finest characters and the truest friends, as noble in their private lives as the former are in public life, have wrung my hand and said, Courage!
And why should I not confess that this friendship, and the testimony here and there of persons unknown to me, have upheld me in my career, both against myself and against unjust attacks; against the calumny which has often persecuted me, against discouragement, and against the too eager hopefulness whose utterances are misinterpreted as those of overwhelming conceit? I had resolved to display stolid stoicism in the face of abuse and insults; but on two occasions base slanders have necessitated a reply. Though the advocates of forgiveness of injuries may regret that I should have displayed my skill in literary fence, there are many Christians who are of opinion that we live in times when it is as well to show sometimes that silence springs from generosity.
The vastness of a plan which includes both a history and a criticism of society, an analysis of its evils, and a discussion of its principles, authorizes me, I think, in giving to my work the title under which it now appears﻿—The Human Comedy. Is this too ambitious? Is it not exact?

===Chinese===

这便是地基，满是演员，满是喜剧与悲剧，在这地基上矗立起《哲学研究》——我作品的第二部分，其中展示这一切效果的社会工具，并逐种情感地描绘心灵的蹂躏；该系列的第一部《驴皮记》，在某种程度上连接着哲学研究与风俗研究，那是一部几乎可称东方奇想的作品，其中展现了生命本身与一切激情的本源之间的殊死搏斗。
除此之外，还将有一系列《分析研究》，对此我不欲多言，因为迄今只出版了一部——《婚姻生理学》。
随着时间的推移，我打算再写两部这类著作：先是《社会生活病理学》，再是《教育机构解剖学》与《美德专论》。
想到尚待完成的一切，我的读者们也许会应和我出版商的话：「愿上帝保佑你活下去！」我只求自开始这项可怕劳作以来，少受一些人与事的折磨，别像我迄今所遭的那样。有一点是对我有利的，我为此感谢上帝：当世的才士、最优秀的人物和最真挚的朋友——他们私生活之高尚，一如前者在公共生活中之高尚——都曾紧握我的手说：拿出勇气来！
我为什么不承认呢：这份友谊，还有素不相识者时时间接给我的见证，支撑着我的写作生涯，既抵抗我自己，也抵抗不公正的攻击；抵抗常常纠缠我的诽谤，抵抗灰心丧气，也抵抗那种被人误解为狂妄自大的急切乐观。我本决心在辱骂与侮辱面前摆出麻木的坚忍；但有两回，卑劣的中伤逼得我不能不回击。虽然宽恕论者也许会惋惜我卖弄了笔墨剑术，但许多基督徒都认为，在我们这个时代，有时不妨让人看到：沉默出自宽宏。
一部计划，既包含社会的历史又包含社会的批评，既分析其弊病又讨论其原则，其规模之宏，我想足使我有权给作品冠以如今这个名目——「人间喜剧」。这过于狂妄吗？难道它不确切吗？

===Original===

That, when it is complete, the public must pronounce.

===Chinese===

这，须待作品完成之后，由公众来裁定。

## At the Sign of the Cat and Racket / 猫打球商店
===Original===

Dedicated to Mademoiselle Marie de Montheau
Halfway down the Rue Saint-Denis, almost at the corner of the Rue du Petit-Lion, there stood formerly one of those delightful houses which enable historians to reconstruct old Paris by analogy. The threatening walls of this tumbledown abode seemed to have been decorated with hieroglyphics. For what other name could the passerby give to the *X*’s and *V*’s which the horizontal or diagonal timbers traced on the front, outlined by little parallel cracks in the plaster? It was evident that every beam quivered in its mortices at the passing of the lightest vehicle. This venerable structure was crowned by a triangular roof of which no example will, ere long, be seen in Paris. This covering, warped by the extremes of the Paris climate, projected three feet over the roadway, as much to protect the threshold from the rainfall as to shelter the wall of a loft and its sill-less dormer-window. This upper story was built of planks, overlapping each other like slates, in order, no doubt, not to overweight the frail house.
One rainy morning in the month of March, a young man, carefully wrapped in his cloak, stood under the awning of a shop opposite this old house, which he was studying with the enthusiasm of an antiquary. In point of fact, this relic of the civic life of the sixteenth century offered more than one problem to the consideration of an observer. Each story presented some singularity; on the first floor four tall, narrow windows, close together, were filled as to the lower panes with boards, so as to produce the doubtful light by which a clever salesman can ascribe to his goods the color his customers inquire for. The young man seemed very scornful of this part of the house; his eyes had not yet rested on it. The windows of the second floor, where the Venetian blinds were drawn up, revealing little dingy muslin curtains behind the large Bohemian glass panes, did not interest him either. His attention was attracted to the third floor, to the modest sash-frames of wood, so clumsily wrought that they might have found a place in the Museum of Arts and Crafts to illustrate the early efforts of French carpentry.

===Chinese===

献给玛丽·德·蒙托小姐
从前，在圣但尼街（Rue Saint-Denis）中段、几乎挨着小狮街（Rue du Petit-Lion）拐角的地方，立着一座讨人喜欢的房子，正是这类房子，让史家得以依样重构旧日的巴黎（Paris）。这座破败老屋的墙壁森然可怖，上面仿佛饰满了象形文字。横梁斜木在正面勾勒出的一个个「X」和「V」，四周又衬着灰泥上的细密平行裂纹，过路人见了，除了这个名目还能叫它什么呢？显然，最轻的车子驶过，每一根梁木都会在榫眼里震颤。这座年代久远、令人肃然起敬的建筑顶上冠着三角形的屋顶，这种式样不久便要在巴黎绝迹了。这层顶盖被巴黎酷烈的气候弄得翘曲歪扭，向街面上方挑出三尺，既为保护门槛免遭雨水，也为遮蔽阁楼的一堵墙和那扇没有窗台的老虎窗。阁楼这层用木板搭成，板子像石板瓦那样层层压茬，无疑是为了不给这孱弱的房子再添重量。
三月里一个落雨的早晨，一个年轻人裹紧披风，站在与老屋相对的一家店铺的雨棚下，正以考古学家般的热情打量着它。事实上，这座十六世纪市民生活的遗物，给观者出的难题不止一个。每一层都各有其古怪之处：二楼四扇又高又窄、挤在一起的窗子，下半截都镶了木板，好造出那种暧昧的光线，精明的伙计便能借此把货色说成顾客要问的任何颜色。年轻人对房子的这一部分似乎很不屑；他的眼睛还不曾落在那里。三楼的窗子，软百叶卷了起来，露出波希米亚大玻璃后面发黄的小平纹纱帘，也引不起他的兴趣。他的注意力被引到了四楼那几扇木框窗上——朴素之极，做工粗笨，简直可以送进工艺博物馆，去做法国木工早期尝试的展品。

===Original===

These windows were glazed with small squares of glass so green that, but for his good eyes, the young man could not have seen the blue-checked cotton curtains which screened the mysteries of the room from profane eyes. Now and then the watcher, weary of his fruitless contemplation, or of the silence in which the house was buried, like the whole neighborhood, dropped his eyes towards the lower regions. An involuntary smile parted his lips each time he looked at the shop, where, in fact, there were some laughable details.
A formidable wooden beam, resting on four pillars, which appeared to have bent under the weight of the decrepit house, had been encrusted with as many coats of different paint as there are of rouge on an old duchess’ cheek. In the middle of this broad and fantastically carved joist there was an old painting representing a cat playing rackets. This picture was what moved the young man to mirth. But it must be said that the wittiest of modern painters could not invent so comical a caricature. The animal held in one of its forepaws a racket as big as itself, and stood on its hind legs to aim at hitting an enormous ball, returned by a man in a fine embroidered coat. Drawing, color, and accessories, all were treated in such a way as to suggest that the artist had meant to make game of the shop-owner and of the passing observer. Time, while impairing this artless painting, had made it yet more grotesque by introducing some uncertain features which must have puzzled the conscientious idler. For instance, the cat’s tail had been eaten into in such a way that it might now have been taken for the figure of a spectator﻿—so long, and thick, and furry were the tails of our forefathers’ cats. To the right of the picture, on an azure field which ill-disguised the decay of the wood, might be read the name “Guillaume,” and to the left, “Successor to Master Chevrel.” Sun and rain had worn away most of the gilding parsimoniously applied to the letters of this superscription, in which the *U*’s and *V*’s had changed places in obedience to the laws of old-world orthography.

===Chinese===

这些窗子镶着一格一格的小方玻璃，绿得厉害，若不是年轻人眼力好，断看不出那遮住房间秘密、不让俗眼窥探的蓝格子布帘。守望的人时不时厌倦于这徒然的凝望，或厌倦于这幢房子乃至整个街区所深陷的寂静，便把眼睛垂向下面的部位。而每逢望见那店铺，他的唇边便不由自主地绽开一丝笑意，因为那里确实有些可笑的细节。
一根粗大的木梁架在四根柱子上，柱子似乎已被老朽的房子的重量压弯；梁上层层敷着各色油漆，之多不亚于老公爵夫人脸上的脂粉。在这根宽阔而雕着古怪花纹的托梁正中，有一幅旧画，画的是一只猫在打球拍。正是这幅画逗乐了年轻人。但必须说，最诙谐的现代画家也造不出这么滑稽的一幅漫画。那畜生前爪抓着一只与它自身一般大的球拍，后腿直立，正要击打一只巨大的球，那球由一个穿绣花礼服的男人回击过来。素描、色彩、配景，一切都处理得叫人觉得画家存心嘲弄店主和过路的看客。岁月剥蚀着这幅质朴的画，又添上几笔含混不清的痕迹，把它弄得更古怪了，想必叫认真的闲人也困惑不已。譬如，猫尾巴被蛀掉了一截，如今倒可以当作一个看客的身影——我们祖辈的猫，尾巴就是那么长、那么粗、毛茸茸的。画面右边，在一片遮不住木头朽坏的蓝色底子上，可以读出「纪尧姆」的名字；左边则是「谢弗勒尔师傅的继任者」。题字上的字母本来吝啬地贴了少许金箔，大都被日晒雨淋磨掉了；那些 U 和 V 又遵照旧时代正字法的规矩互换了位置。

===Original===

To quench the pride of those who believe that the world is growing cleverer day by day, and that modern humbug surpasses everything, it may be observed that these signs, of which the origin seems so whimsical to many Paris merchants, are the dead pictures of once living pictures by which our roguish ancestors contrived to tempt customers into their houses. Thus the Spinning Sow, the Green Monkey, and others, were animals in cages whose skills astonished the passerby, and whose accomplishments prove the patience of the fifteenth-century artisan. Such curiosities did more to enrich their fortunate owners than the signs of “Providence,” “Good-faith,” “Grace of God,” and “Decapitation of John the Baptist,” which may still be seen in the Rue Saint-Denis.
However, our stranger was certainly not standing there to admire the cat, which a minute’s attention sufficed to stamp on his memory. The young man himself had his peculiarities. His cloak, folded after the manner of an antique drapery, showed a smart pair of shoes, all the more remarkable in the midst of the Paris mud, because he wore white silk stockings, on which the splashes betrayed his impatience. He had just come, no doubt, from a wedding or a ball; for at this early hour he had in his hand a pair of white gloves, and his black hair, now out of curl, and flowing over his shoulders, showed that it had been dressed à la Caracalla, a fashion introduced as much by David’s school of painting as by the mania for Greek and Roman styles which characterized the early years of this century.
In spite of the noise made by a few market gardeners, who, being late, rattled past towards the great marketplace at a gallop, the busy street lay in a stillness of which the magic charm is known only to those who have wandered through deserted Paris at the hours when its roar, hushed for a moment, rises and spreads in the distance like the great voice of the sea. This strange young man must have seemed as curious to the shopkeeping folk of the Cat and Racket as the Cat and Racket was to him. A dazzlingly white cravat made his anxious face look even paler than it really was. The fire that flashed in his black eyes, gloomy and sparkling by turns, was in harmony with the singular outline of his features, with his wide, flexible mouth, hardened into a smile. His forehead, knit with violent annoyance, had a stamp of doom.

===Chinese===

有些人相信世界一天比一天聪明，现代的招摇撞骗胜过一切；要灭一灭这种傲气，不妨指出：这些招牌——在许多巴黎商人看来来历何等古怪——原是往昔活画面的死摹本，我们狡黠的祖先正是靠那些活画面引诱顾客进门的。譬如「纺线的母猪」「绿猴」等等，原是笼中的动物，它们的技艺叫行人惊叹，它们的本领也证明着十五世纪工匠的耐心。这类奇货给幸运的店主带来的进项，远胜于「天意」「诚信」「神恩」「圣约翰斩首」之类至今仍可在圣但尼街见到的招牌。
不过，我们这位陌生人站在那里，当然不是为了欣赏那只猫——那猫他只消看上一分钟便已铭记在心。年轻人自己也有他的古怪之处。他的披风按古代衣褶的样式裹着，露出一双讲究的鞋；他穿着白丝袜，在这巴黎的泥泞中格外惹眼，袜上的泥点又泄露了他的焦躁。他想必刚从一场婚礼或舞会上出来；因为这么一大早，他手里还捏着一副白手套，他那头黑发——如今已经散乱，披在肩上——看得出原是梳成「卡拉卡拉」式的，这个发式一半由大卫的画派、一半由本世纪初那种崇尚希腊罗马风尚的狂热带动起来。
几个赶晚了的菜农驾着车朝大市场疾驰而过，铿铿作响；但除此之外，这条繁忙的街还笼罩在一种寂静里，其魔力只有那些在巴黎人踪寥落之时漫步城中的人才知道——那时巴黎的喧嚣短暂地沉寂下去，又在远方升起、扩散，如同大海的宏声。在猫打球商店的店家眼里，这个古怪的年轻人想必和猫打球商店在他眼里一样古怪。一条白得耀眼的领巾把他那焦虑的脸衬得比实际更苍白。他黑眼睛里忽而阴郁、忽而闪亮的火光，与他五官的奇特轮廓正相称，与他那宽阔、灵活、此刻僵作一个笑容的嘴正相称。他的额头因盛怒而紧锁，带着一种宿命的印记。

===Original===

Is not the forehead the most prophetic feature of a man? When the stranger’s brow expressed passion the furrows formed in it were terrible in their strength and energy; but when he recovered his calmness, so easily upset, it beamed with a luminous grace which gave great attractiveness to a countenance in which joy, grief, love, anger, or scorn blazed out so contagiously that the coldest man could not fail to be impressed.
He was so thoroughly vexed by the time when the dormer-window of the loft was suddenly flung open, that he did not observe the apparition of three laughing faces, pink and white and chubby, but as vulgar as the face of Commerce as it is seen in sculpture on certain monuments. These three faces, framed by the window, recalled the puffy cherubs floating among the clouds that surround God the Father. The apprentices snuffed up the exhalations of the street with an eagerness that showed how hot and poisonous the atmosphere of their garret must be. After pointing to the singular sentinel, the most jovial, as he seemed, of the apprentices retired and came back holding an instrument whose hard metal pipe is now superseded by a leather tube; and they all grinned with mischief as they looked down on the loiterer, and sprinkled him with a fine white shower of which the scent proved that three chins had just been shaved. Standing on tiptoe, in the farthest corner of their loft, to enjoy their victim’s rage, the lads ceased laughing on seeing the haughty indifference with which the young man shook his cloak, and the intense contempt expressed by his face as he glanced up at the empty window-frame.
At this moment a slender white hand threw up the lower half of one of the clumsy windows on the third floor by the aid of the sash runners, of which the pulley so often suddenly gives way and releases the heavy panes it ought to hold up. The watcher was then rewarded for his long waiting. The face of a young girl appeared, as fresh as one of the white cups that bloom on the bosom of the waters, crowned by a frill of tumbled muslin, which gave her head a look of exquisite innocence. Though wrapped in brown stuff, her neck and shoulders gleamed here and there through little openings left by her movements in sleep.

===Chinese===

额头难道不是人脸上最有预言性的部分吗？当这位陌生人的额头表露激情时，那上面刻下的皱纹，其力度与劲道咄咄逼人；可当他恢复——那么容易失去的——平静时，额头便焕发出一种明朗的优雅，使这张脸极有魅力：喜悦、悲伤、爱情、愤怒或轻蔑，都在这张脸上燃烧得那么富于感染力，最冷漠的人也不能无所触动。
阁楼的老虎窗突然推开时，他正烦恼到极点，竟没有留意三张笑脸的出现——粉红白胖，却俗气十足，就像某些纪念碑雕塑上的「商业」之神的脸。这三张脸嵌在窗框里，叫人想起浮在圣父周围云朵间那些胖乎乎的小天使。学徒们贪婪地吸着街上的空气，那股急切劲儿足见他们阁楼里的空气多么闷热、多么浊臭。指过那个古怪的哨兵之后，学徒中看似最快活的一个退了下去，回来时拿着一件家什——那种硬金属嘴的物件，如今已被皮管取代了；他们俯视着那个游荡者，个个坏笑着，向他洒下一阵细细的白沫，那气味表明三副下巴刚刚刮过胡子。几个小伙子踮起脚尖，缩在阁楼最里面的角落里，等着欣赏受害者的火气；可一见年轻人抖披风时那股高傲的冷漠、他抬眼望向空窗框时脸上那浓浓的轻蔑，他们便笑不出来了。
就在这时，一只纤细白皙的手借着窗框滑轮，推开了四楼一扇笨重窗子的下半扇——那滑轮常常突然一脱，松开它本应吊住的沉重窗格。守望者漫长的等待就此得到了报偿。一张年轻姑娘的脸出现了，鲜嫩得如同开放在水面上的一朵白杯花，头上覆着一圈揉皱的细纱褶边，使她的头显出一种精致的稚气。她虽裹着棕色粗呢，脖颈和肩膀却在睡姿弄开的缝隙间这里那里地闪着微光。

===Original===

No expression of embarrassment detracted from the candor of her face, or the calm look of eyes immortalized long since in the sublime works of Raphael; here were the same grace, the same repose as in those Virgins, and now proverbial. There was a delightful contrast between the cheeks of that face on which sleep had, as it were, given high relief to a superabundance of life, and the antiquity of the heavy window with its clumsy shape and black sill. Like those day-blowing flowers, which in the early morning have not yet unfurled their cups, twisted by the chills of night, the girl, as yet hardly awake, let her blue eyes wander beyond the neighboring roofs to look at the sky; then, from habit, she cast them down on the gloomy depths of the street, where they immediately met those of her adorer. Vanity, no doubt, distressed her at being seen in undress; she started back, the worn pulley gave way, and the sash fell with the rapid run, which in our day has earned for this artless invention of our forefathers an odious name.1 The vision had disappeared. To the young man the most radiant star of morning seemed to be hidden by a cloud.
During these little incidents the heavy inside shutters that protected the slight windows of the shop of the Cat and Racket had been removed as if by magic. The old door with its knocker was opened back against the wall of the entry by a manservant, apparently coeval with the sign, who, with a shaking hand, hung upon it a square of cloth, on which were embroidered in yellow silk the words: “Guillaume, successor to Chevrel.” Many a passerby would have found it difficult to guess the class of trade carried on by Monsieur Guillaume. Between the strong iron bars which protected his shop windows on the outside, certain packages, wrapped in brown linen, were hardly visible, though as numerous as herrings swimming in a shoal. Notwithstanding the primitive aspect of the Gothic front, Monsieur Guillaume, of all the merchant clothiers in Paris, was the one whose stores were always the best provided, whose connections were the most extensive, and whose commercial honesty never lay under the slightest suspicion. If some of his brethren in business made a contract with the Government, and had not the required quantity of cloth, he was always ready to deliver it, however large the number of pieces tendered for.

她脸上没有一丝慌乱的痕迹损及那份坦然，那双眼睛的安详目光，早已在拉斐尔的崇高作品里成为不朽；这里有着与那些圣母像同样的优雅、同样的宁静，如今已成人间共赏的典范。那张脸上，睡眠仿佛把过盛的生命雕成了高浮雕；这面容与那扇笨重黝黑、形制古旧的窗子之间，构成一种令人愉悦的对照。就像那些白天开放的花儿，清晨里还未舒展开被夜寒扭卷的花杯，姑娘也还半睡半醒，任她那双蓝眼睛越过邻近的屋顶眺望天空；然后，出于习惯，她把目光垂到街上幽暗的深处，立刻与她的爱慕者的目光相遇了。被人看见衣衫未整，虚荣心——想必是——让她着慌了；她猛地缩回去，磨损的滑轮一脱，窗扇带着那种疾坠落下，正是这种疾坠，使我们今天给祖先这一质朴的发明冠上了一个可憎的名字(1)。幻影消失了。在年轻人看来，清晨最明亮的星辰仿佛被一片云遮住了。
就在这些小小的插曲进行时，护着猫打球商店单薄橱窗的沉重内板窗，已像变戏法似的卸了下来。那个与招牌仿佛同龄的男仆，用颤抖的手把一方布挂在装门环的老门上——布上用黄丝线绣着：「纪尧姆，谢弗勒尔的继任者」。许多过路人怕是难以猜出纪尧姆先生做的是哪一行的买卖。在保护橱窗外面的粗铁条之间，一些裹着棕色亚麻布的包裹几乎看不见，数量却多得像浅滩里的鲱鱼。尽管哥特式的门面一派古旧气象，巴黎的呢绒商中，铺货最充足、关系最广、商业信誉从未受到丝毫怀疑的，正是纪尧姆先生。同行中若有人与政府签了合同而凑不齐所需数量的呢料，无论要多少匹，他总能供货。

===Original===

The wily dealer knew a thousand ways of extracting the largest profits without being obliged, like them, to court patrons, cringing to them, or making them costly presents. When his fellow-tradesmen could only pay in good bills of long date, he would mention his notary as an accommodating man, and managed to get a second profit out of the bargain, thanks to this arrangement, which had made it a proverb among the traders of the Rue Saint-Denis: “Heaven preserve you from Monsieur Guillaume’s notary!” to signify a heavy discount.
The old merchant was to be seen standing on the threshold of his shop, as if by a miracle, the instant the servant withdrew. Monsieur Guillaume looked at the Rue Saint-Denis, at the neighboring shops, and at the weather, like a man disembarking at Havre, and seeing France once more after a long voyage. Having convinced himself that nothing had changed while he was asleep, he presently perceived the stranger on guard, and he, on his part, gazed at the patriarchal draper as Humboldt may have scrutinized the first electric eel he saw in America. Monsieur Guillaume wore loose black velvet breeches, pepper-and-salt stockings, and square toed shoes with silver buckles. His coat, with square-cut fronts, square-cut tails, and square-cut collar clothed his slightly bent figure in greenish cloth, finished with white metal buttons, tawny from wear. His gray hair was so accurately combed and flattened over his yellow pate that it made it look like a furrowed field. His little green eyes, that might have been pierced with a gimlet, flashed beneath arches faintly tinged with red in the place of eyebrows. Anxieties had wrinkled his forehead with as many horizontal lines as there were creases in his coat. This colorless face expressed patience, commercial shrewdness, and the sort of wily cupidity which is needful in business. At that time these old families were less rare than they are now, in which the characteristic habits and costume of their calling, surviving in the midst of more recent civilization, were preserved as cherished traditions, like the antediluvian remains found by Cuvier in the quarries.
The head of the Guillaume family was a notable upholder of ancient practices; he might be heard to regret the Provost of Merchants, and never did he mention a decision of the Tribunal of Commerce without calling it the *Sentence of the Consuls*.

===Chinese===

这个精明的商人自有一千种牟取最大利润的法子，用不着像同行那样巴结主顾、折腰奉承或奉上贵重的礼物。当同行只能拿长期的好票据支付时，他便提起自己的公证人，说他是个通融的人，设法从这笔买卖里再赚一道——多亏这套安排，圣但尼街的商人间流传开一句谚语：「愿上天保佑你别碰上纪尧姆先生的公证人！」意即狠打折扣。
仆人一退下去，老商人便仿佛奇迹一般出现在店铺门槛上。纪尧姆先生望着圣但尼街、望着左右的铺子、望着天色，像一个刚在勒阿弗尔上岸、远航归来重见法兰西的人。确信自己睡着的时候一切照旧之后，他随即发觉了守望着的陌生人；而陌生人这一边，也像洪堡端详他在美洲见到的第一条电鳗那样端详着这位族长般的呢绒商。纪尧姆先生穿着宽松的黑丝绒短裤、椒盐色的长袜、缀银扣的方头鞋。他那件上衣，方角的门襟、方角的下摆、方角的领子，用泛绿的呢料裹着他微驼的身躯，缀着白铜纽扣，磨得发黄。他的灰发在蜡黄的头顶上梳得平平整整、一丝不苟，使头顶看上去像一块犁过的田。两只绿莹莹的小眼睛——简直像用钻头钻出来的——在代作眉毛的淡淡发红的眼眶下闪烁。操劳在他额头上犁出的一道道横纹，同他外衣上的褶子一样多。这张没有血色的脸上，写着耐心、商人的精明，以及生意场上必不可少的那种狡黠的贪心。那时候，这类旧家还不像如今这样稀少：行业的特有习尚与装束，在较新的文明中间留存下来，被当作珍贵的传统保存着，就像居维叶在采石场里发现的洪水期以前的遗骸。
纪尧姆家的家长是古老公道的一名著名的维护者；可以听见他惋惜「商人会长」的制度；他提到商事法庭的判决，从来只叫它「执政们的裁决」。

===Original===

Up and dressed the first of the household, in obedience, no doubt, to these old customs, he stood sternly awaiting the appearance of his three assistants, ready to scold them in case they were late. These young disciples of Mercury knew nothing more terrible than the wordless assiduity with which the master scrutinized their faces and their movements on Monday in search of evidence or traces of their pranks. But at this moment the old clothier paid no heed to his apprentices; he was absorbed in trying to divine the motive of the anxious looks which the young man in silk stockings and a cloak cast alternately at his signboard and into the depths of his shop. The daylight was now brighter, and enabled the stranger to discern the cashier’s corner enclosed by a railing and screened by old green silk curtains, where were kept the immense ledgers, the silent oracles of the house. The too inquisitive gazer seemed to covet this little nook, and to be taking the plan of a dining-room at one side, lighted by a skylight, whence the family at meals could easily see the smallest incident that might occur at the shop-door. So much affection for his dwelling seemed suspicious to a trader who had lived long enough to remember the law of maximum prices; Monsieur Guillaume naturally thought that this sinister personage had an eye to the till of the Cat and Racket. After quietly observing the mute duel which was going on between his master and the stranger, the eldest of the apprentices, having seen that the young man was stealthily watching the windows of the third floor, ventured to place himself on the stone flag where Monsieur Guillaume was standing. He took two steps out into the street, raised his head, and fancied that he caught sight of Mademoiselle Augustine Guillaume in hasty retreat. The draper, annoyed by his assistant’s perspicacity, shot a side glance at him; but the draper and his amorous apprentice were suddenly relieved from the fears which the young man’s presence had excited in their minds. He hailed a hackney cab on its way to a neighboring stand, and jumped into it with an air of affected indifference. This departure was a balm to the hearts of the other two lads, who had been somewhat uneasy as to meeting the victim of their practical joke.
“Well, gentlemen, what ails you that you are standing there with your arms folded?”

===Chinese===

他照这些老规矩，无疑总是全家最先起身穿戴整齐的一个，此刻正严厉地等着三个伙计露面，预备在他们迟到时训斥一顿。这些墨丘利的年轻门徒最怕的，莫过于每逢星期一，师父对他们脸上身上那番无声的细察，要从里面找出他们恶作剧的迹象或痕迹。但这时候，老呢绒商没有理会学徒们；他一心想猜透那个穿丝袜披披风的年轻人交替投向他的招牌和店铺深处的焦灼目光用意何在。天光如今更亮了，陌生人已能看清用栏杆围起、挂着旧绿绸帘的账房角落，那里存放着这家商号的大账本——沉默的先知。这位过分好奇的凝望者似乎觊觎着这个小小的角落，还在打量旁边一间开着天窗的饭厅，一家人吃饭时，从那里能把店门口发生的最小的事故尽收眼底。对一个活得够久、还记得最高限价法令的商人来说，对本店房屋这么深的情意便显得可疑；纪尧姆先生自然而然地认定，这个阴沉的人物盯上了猫打球商店的钱柜。大伙计悄悄观察了一会儿师父与陌生人之间进行的那场哑战，看清了年轻人正偷觑着四楼的窗子，便斗胆站到纪尧姆先生立着的那块石板上。他向街上跨出两步，抬起头，仿佛瞥见奥古斯丁·纪尧姆（Augustine Guillaume）小姐仓皇退走的背影。呢绒商被伙计的眼力弄得很不痛快，斜眼瞪了他一下；可是，师徒二人——商人和他那位害相思的学徒——忽然都从年轻人现身引起的担心中解脱出来：他招手唤住一辆正驶往附近停车处的出租马车，装出一副满不在乎的神气跳了上去。这一走，对另外两个小伙子是一帖宽心药，他们正为会撞上那场恶作剧的受害者而有点忐忑呢。
「喂，先生们，你们站在那儿抱着胳膊，是中了什么邪？」

===Original===

said Monsieur Guillaume to his three neophytes. “In former days, bless you, when I was in Master Chevrel’s service, I should have overhauled more than two pieces of cloth by this time.”
“Then it was daylight earlier,” said the second assistant, whose duty this was.
The old shopkeeper could not help smiling. Though two of these young fellows, who were confided to his care by their fathers, rich manufacturers at Louviers and at Sedan, had only to ask and to have a hundred thousand francs the day when they were old enough to settle in life, Guillaume regarded it as his duty to keep them under the rod of an old-world despotism, unknown nowadays in the showy modern shops, where the apprentices expect to be rich men at thirty. He made them work like Negroes. These three assistants were equal to a business which would harry ten such clerks as those whose sybaritical tastes now swell the columns of the budget. Not a sound disturbed the peace of this solemn house, where the hinges were always oiled, and where the meanest article of furniture showed the respectable cleanliness which reveals strict order and economy. The most waggish of the three youths often amused himself by writing the date of its first appearance on the Gruyère cheese which was left to their tender mercies at breakfast, and which it was their pleasure to leave untouched. This bit of mischief, and a few others of the same stamp, would sometimes bring a smile on the face of the younger of Guillaume’s daughters, the pretty maiden who has just now appeared to the bewitched man in the street.
Though each of these apprentices, even the eldest, paid a round sum for his board, not one of them would have been bold enough to remain at the master’s table when dessert was served. When Madame Guillaume talked of dressing the salad, the hapless youths trembled as they thought of the thrift with which her prudent hand dispensed the oil. They could never think of spending a night away from the house without having given, long before, a plausible reason for such an irregularity. Every Sunday, each in his turn, two of them accompanied the Guillaume family to Mass at Saint-Leu, and to vespers.

===Chinese===

纪尧姆先生对三个新入门的徒弟说。「想当年，天哪，我在谢弗勒尔师傅手下当差的时候，到这个钟点，两匹以上的呢料早就翻检过了。」
「那是从前天亮得早。」二伙计说——顶这句嘴本来就是他的职分。
老店主禁不住笑了。这三个年轻人中，有两个的父亲是卢维耶和色当的富厂主，把儿子托付给他照管；这两个小伙子只消开口，到了成家立业的年纪便有十万法郎可用；但尽管如此，纪尧姆仍认为自己的本分是拿旧式的专制管教压着他们，那套管教如今在时新的豪华铺子里已无人知晓——那里的学徒三十岁上就指望当富翁了。他叫他们像黑奴一样干活。这三个伙计抵得上够十个那样职员忙的买卖——如今正是那些职员的骄奢口味撑大了预算的开支。这庄重的人家没有任何声响搅扰它的安宁：门铰链永远上着油，最不起眼的家具也透着可敬的洁净，显示着严格的秩序与节俭。三个青年中最淘气的一个常拿早餐时听凭他们发落的格吕耶尔奶酪开心——在奶酪上写下它初次露面的日期，他们乐于一口不动。这类小小的恶作剧，还有另外几桩同类的把戏，有时会引得纪尧姆的小女儿——就是方才在街上令那个着迷的人一见的那位漂亮姑娘——嫣然一笑。
尽管这几个学徒，连大伙计在内，人人都为膳宿付着一笔可观的费用，上甜点的时候却没有一个敢斗胆留在东家的桌上。每当纪尧姆太太（Madame Guillaume）说要拌生菜，不幸的青年们便打颤，想到她那只节俭的手倒油时何等斤斤计较。他们若想在外头过一夜，不早早交出一个像样的理由说明这种越轨，那是想也不用想的。每个星期日，三人轮流，总有两个陪同纪尧姆一家去圣勒乌望弥撒，再望晚祷。

===Original===

Mesdemoiselles Virginie and Augustine, simply attired in cotton print, each took the arm of an apprentice and walked in front, under the piercing eye of their mother, who closed the little family procession with her husband, accustomed by her to carry two large prayerbooks, bound in black morocco. The second apprentice received no salary. As for the eldest, whose twelve years of perseverance and discretion had initiated him into the secrets of the house, he was paid eight hundred francs a year as the reward of his labors. On certain family festivals he received as a gratuity some little gift, to which Madame Guillaume’s dry and wrinkled hand alone gave value﻿—netted purses, which she took care to stuff with cotton wool, to show off the fancy stitches, braces of the strongest make, or heavy silk stockings. Sometimes, but rarely, this prime minister was admitted to share the pleasures of the family when they went into the country, or when, after waiting for months, they made up their mind to exert the right acquired by taking a box at the theatre to command a piece which Paris had already forgotten.
As to the other assistants, the barrier of respect which formerly divided a master draper from his apprentices was that they would have been more likely to steal a piece of cloth than to infringe this time-honored etiquette. Such reserve may now appear ridiculous; but these old houses were a school of honesty and sound morals. The masters adopted their apprentices. The young man’s linen was cared for, mended, and often replaced by the mistress of the house. If an apprentice fell ill, he was the object of truly maternal attention. In a case of danger the master lavished his money in calling in the most celebrated physicians, for he was not answerable to their parents merely for the good conduct and training of the lads. If one of them, whose character was unimpeachable, suffered misfortune, these old tradesmen knew how to value the intelligence he had displayed, and they did not hesitate to entrust the happiness of their daughters to men whom they had long trusted with their fortunes. Guillaume was one of these men of the old school, and if he had their ridiculous side, he had all their good qualities; and Joseph Lebas, the chief assistant, an orphan without any fortune, was in his mind destined to be the husband of Virginie, his elder daughter.

维尔日妮和奥古斯丁两位小姐穿着朴素的印花布衣裳，各自挽着一个学徒的手臂走在前面，母亲的目光锐利地盯着她们；母亲和父亲殿后，结束这一小小的家庭行列——父亲被她调教惯了，捧着两本黑摩洛哥皮烫面的大祈祷书。二伙计没有薪水。至于大伙计，他十二年的坚忍与谨慎已使他得以参与这一家的机密，每年拿八百法郎作为劳酬。逢到某些家族节庆，他还会得到一点小礼物作赏钱——只是这些东西唯有纪尧姆太太那只干瘪起皱的手才赋予其价值：编织的钱袋，她必定塞满棉絮好显出花针的功夫；结得最牢的背带，或是厚实的丝袜。有时——但很少有——这位「首相」也获准分享全家的乐趣：他们下乡游玩的时候，或是等上几个月、终于下定决心行使订了包厢便可以点戏的权利，点一出巴黎早已忘掉的戏的时候。
至于其余的伙计，从前隔开呢绒商东家与学徒的那道敬重的藩篱，高到这样的地步：他们宁肯去偷一匹呢料，也不敢触犯这源远流长的礼法。这种拘板在今天看来也许可笑；但这些老字号却是一所诚实与正派的学校。东家把学徒当养子。青年的衬衣有人照管、缝补，还常由主妇出面更换。学徒若病了，便受到真正慈母般的照料。遇有危险，东家不惜重金请来最有名的医生，因为对这青年的品行与教养，他向其父母所负的责任可不只这一层。倘若他们中有一个品行无可指摘的人遭了不幸，这些老商人懂得珍视他表现出来的才干，而且毫不犹豫地把女儿的幸福托付给久已托付过财产的人。纪尧姆便是这种旧派人物中的一个，虽有他们可笑的一面，却也兼有他们全部的美德；大伙计约瑟夫·勒巴，一个没有任何财产的孤儿，在他心里早已内定为长女维尔日妮的丈夫。

But Joseph did not share the symmetrical ideas of his master, who would not for an empire have given his second daughter in marriage before the elder. The unhappy assistant felt that his heart was wholly given to Mademoiselle Augustine, the younger. In order to justify this passion, which had grown up in secret, it is necessary to inquire a little further into the springs of the absolute government which ruled the old cloth-merchant’s household.
Guillaume had two daughters. The elder, Mademoiselle Virginie, was the very image of her mother. Madame Guillaume, daughter of the Sieur Chevrel, sat so upright in the stool behind her desk, that more than once she had heard some wag bet that she was a stuffed figure. Her long, thin face betrayed exaggerated piety. Devoid of attractions or of amiable manners, Madame Guillaume commonly decorated her head﻿—that of a woman near on sixty﻿—with a cap of a particular and unvarying shape, with long lappets, like that of a widow. In all the neighborhood she was known as the “portress nun.” Her speech was curt, and her movements had the stiff precision of a semaphore. Her eye, with a gleam in it like a cat’s, seemed to spite the world because she was so ugly. Mademoiselle Virginie, brought up, like her younger sister, under the domestic rule of her mother, had reached the age of eight-and-twenty. Youth mitigated the graceless effect which her likeness to her mother sometimes gave to her features, but maternal austerity had endowed her with two great qualities which made up for everything. She was patient and gentle. Mademoiselle Augustine, who was but just eighteen, was not like either her father or her mother. She was one of those daughters whose total absence of any physical affinity with their parents makes one believe in the adage: “God gives children.” Augustine was little, or, to describe her more truly, delicately made. Full of gracious candor, a man of the world could have found no fault in the charming girl beyond a certain meanness of gesture or vulgarity of attitude, and sometimes a want of ease. Her silent and placid face was full of the transient melancholy which comes over all young girls who are too weak to dare to resist their mother’s will.

可是约瑟夫并不赞同师父那种讲究长幼对称的观念——哪怕给他一个帝国，他也不肯让次女先于长女出嫁。这个不幸的伙计觉得，自己的心已经完全系在妹妹奥古斯丁小姐身上了。为了说明这段暗地里滋生的恋情，有必要再深入探究一番统治着老呢绒商家里的那套专制政府的发条。
纪尧姆有两个女儿。姐姐维尔日妮小姐活脱是母亲的翻版。纪尧姆太太是谢弗勒尔先生的女儿，坐在账台后的凳子上腰板笔直，不止一次听见有促狭鬼打赌说她是蜡人。她那瘦长的脸透着一股过分的虔敬。纪尧姆太太既无动人之处，也无和蔼的举止，通常在头上——那颗年近六十的头——扣一顶式样一成不变、垂着长耳带的软帽，如同寡妇的装束。左邻右舍都管她叫「门房修女」。她说话生硬，一举一动带着信号机般的僵直和准确。她的眼睛闪着猫眼般的光，仿佛因为自己长得这么丑而在跟全世界赌气。维尔日妮小姐同妹妹一样是在母亲的治家之道下长大的，已经二十八岁了。青春冲淡了她酷似母亲的面貌有时给人的生硬之感；而母亲的严峻倒赋予她两大美德，足以补赎一切：她有耐心，性情温柔。奥古斯丁小姐刚满十八岁，既不像父亲，也不像母亲。她是那种与父母在形貌上毫无相似之处的女儿，叫人不能不信那句谚语：「孩子是上帝赐的。」奥古斯丁个子矮小，或者更确切地说，长得纤巧。她满身天真的爽朗；上流社会的人在这位可爱的姑娘身上挑不出别的毛病，只有举手投足间某种小家子气或姿态的俗气，以及偶尔的局促。她那张沉静温和的脸上，浮着一种转瞬即逝的忧郁，凡是太软弱、不敢反抗母命的少女，个个都被这种忧郁笼罩过。

The two sisters, always plainly dressed, could not gratify the innate vanity of womanhood but by a luxury of cleanliness which became them wonderfully, and made them harmonize with the polished counters and the shining shelves, on which the old manservant never left a speck of dust, and with the old-world simplicity of all they saw about them. As their style of living compelled them to find the elements of happiness in persistent work, Augustine and Virginie had hitherto always satisfied their mother, who secretly prided herself on the perfect characters of her two daughters. It is easy to imagine the results of the training they had received. Brought up to a commercial life, accustomed to hear nothing but dreary arguments and calculations about trade, having studied nothing but grammar, bookkeeping, a little Bible-history, and the history of France in *Le Ragois*, and never reading any book but what their mother would sanction, their ideas had not acquired much scope. They knew perfectly how to keep house; they were familiar with the prices of things; they understood the difficulty of amassing money; they were economical, and had a great respect for the qualities that make a man of business. Although their father was rich, they were as skilled in darning as in embroidery; their mother often talked of having them taught to cook, so that they might know how to order a dinner and scold a cook with due knowledge. They knew nothing of the pleasures of the world; and, seeing how their parents spent their exemplary lives, they very rarely suffered their eyes to wander beyond the walls of their hereditary home, which to their mother was the whole universe. The meetings to which family anniversaries gave rise filled in the future of earthly joy to them.

姐妹俩衣着永远朴素，能满足女性天生的虚荣心的，唯有洁净这份奢华——这于她们再相宜不过，使她们与擦得镫亮的柜台、照得见人的货架彼此协调（老男仆从不让架子上留一粒灰尘），也与她们目之所及的一派旧式简朴相协调。她们的生活方式迫使她们在不懈的劳作中寻觅幸福的要素；奥古斯丁和维尔日妮迄今总是让母亲称心，母亲则暗自为两个女儿完美的品性而自豪。她们所受调教的结果不难想见。她们受的是买卖人的教养，听惯的尽是生意上枯燥的争论和计算，学过的只有语法、簿记、一点圣经纪事，还有拉古瓦编的法兰西史，读的书又从不出母亲圈定的范围，因此见识不曾开阔到哪里去。她们极会当家；对各样东西的行情了如指掌；懂得积攒钱财之不易；节俭，而且极敬重那种成就一个生意人的品质。虽然父亲富有，她们补袜子的手艺不亚于刺绣；母亲常说要教她们烧菜，好让她们懂得如何点一桌菜，也懂得如何在行地训斥厨娘。世上的欢乐她们一概不知；眼看父母过着堪为楷模的生活，她们极少让眼睛越过祖宅的院墙——在那母亲眼里，这宅子就是整个宇宙。家族纪念日带来的聚会，便填满了她们尘世幸福的全部未来。

When the great drawing-room on the second floor was to be prepared to receive company﻿—Madame Roguin, a Demoiselle Chevrel, fifteen months younger than her cousin, and bedecked with diamonds; young Rabourdin, employed in the Finance Office; Monsieur Cesar Birotteau, the rich perfumer, and his wife, known as Madame Cesar; Monsieur Camusot, the richest silk mercer in the Rue des Bourdonnais, with his father-in-law, Monsieur Cardot, two or three old bankers, and some immaculate ladies﻿—the arrangements, made necessary by the way in which everything was packed away﻿—the plate, the Dresden china, the candlesticks, and the glass﻿—made a variety in the monotonous lives of the three women, who came and went and exerted themselves as nuns would to receive their bishop. Then, in the evening, when all three were tired out with having wiped, rubbed, unpacked, and arranged all the gauds of the festival, as the girls helped their mother to undress, Madame Guillaume would say to them, “Children, we have done nothing today.”
When, on very great occasions, “the portress nun” allowed dancing, restricting the games of boston, whist, and backgammon within the limits of her bedroom, such a concession was accounted as the most unhoped felicity, and made them happier than going to the great balls, to two or three of which Guillaume would take the girls at the time of the Carnival.
And once a year the worthy draper gave an entertainment, when he spared no expense. However rich and fashionable the persons invited might be, they were careful not to be absent; for the most important houses on the exchange had recourse to the immense credit, the fortune, or the time-honored experience of Monsieur Guillaume. Still, the excellent merchant’s daughters did not benefit as much as might be supposed by the lessons the world has to offer to young spirits. At these parties, which were indeed set down in the ledger to the credit of the house, they wore dresses the shabbiness of which made them blush. Their style of dancing was not in any way remarkable, and their mother’s surveillance did not allow of their holding any conversation with their partners beyond Yes and No. Also, the law of the old sign of the Cat and Racket commanded that they should be home by eleven o’clock, the hour when balls and fêtes begin to be lively.

三楼那间大客厅要收拾出来待客的时候——客人有罗甘太太，她是谢弗勒尔家的闺女，比表妹小十五个月，浑身缀满钻石；有财政部的青年拉布尔丹；有富有的香水商塞萨尔·比罗托先生和他那位人称塞萨尔太太的妻子；有布尔多内街最阔的绸缎商卡缪索先生及其岳父卡尔多先生，还有两三位老银行家和几位一尘不染的太太——由于所有东西——银器、德累斯顿瓷器、烛台和玻璃器皿——都收藏得严严实实，这一番筹备便给三个女人单调的生活带来了变化，她们跑前跑后、卖力张罗，像修女迎候主教一般。到了晚上，三人擦的擦、揩的揩、拆的拆、摆的摆，把节日的花花绿绿都归置妥帖，累得筋疲力尽；姑娘们伺候母亲解衣就寝时，纪尧姆太太会对她们说：「孩子们，咱们今天什么事也没干。」
遇上极大的盛典，「门房修女」允许跳舞，把波士顿牌、惠斯特牌和十五子棋限制在自己卧房的限度之内，这样的恩典便被当作天外飞来的幸福，比去参加盛大舞会还教她们快活——狂欢节期间，纪尧姆总要带姑娘们去两三场那样的舞会。
这位可敬的呢绒商每年也设一次宴，届时不惜工本。被邀的客人无论多么有钱有派头，都小心不敢缺席；因为交易所里最有实力的商号，也都要借助纪尧姆先生雄厚的信用、殷实的家财或久经世故的经验。不过，这位杰出商人的女儿们，从世人所能给年轻心灵的教益中得到的，并不像人们想象的那样多。在这些宴会上——它们确实被记在了账上算作商号的开支——她们穿着寒酸的衣裙，臊得脸红。她们的舞步毫无出众之处，母亲的监视也不容她们与舞伴交谈，除了「是」与「不」，再没有别的话。再者，猫打球这块老招牌的家法规定：十一点前必须回家——而十一点，正是舞会和盛会开始热闹起来的时辰。

Thus their pleasures, which seemed to conform very fairly to their father’s position, were often made insipid by circumstances which were part of the family habits and principles.
As to their usual life, one remark will sufficiently paint it. Madame Guillaume required her daughters to be dressed very early in the morning, to come down every day at the same hour, and she ordered their employments with monastic regularity. Augustine, however, had been gifted by chance with a spirit lofty enough to feel the emptiness of such a life. Her blue eyes would sometimes be raised as if to pierce the depths of that gloomy staircase and those damp storerooms. After sounding the profound cloistral silence, she seemed to be listening to remote, inarticulate revelations of the life of passion, which accounts feelings as of higher value than things. And at such moments her cheek would flush, her idle hands would lay the muslin sewing on the polished oak counter, and presently her mother would say in a voice, of which even the softest tones were sour, “Augustine, my treasure, what are you thinking about?” It is possible that two romances discovered by Augustine in the cupboard of a cook Madame Guillaume had lately discharged﻿—*Hippolyte Comte de Douglas* and *Le Comte de Comminges*﻿—may have contributed to develop the ideas of the young girl, who had devoured them in secret, during the long nights of the past winter.
And so Augustine’s expression of vague longing, her gentle voice, her jasmine skin, and her blue eyes had lighted in poor Lebas’ soul a flame as ardent as it was reverent. From an easily understood caprice, Augustine felt no affection for the orphan; perhaps she did not know that he loved her. On the other hand, the senior apprentice, with his long legs, his chestnut hair, his big hands and powerful frame, had found a secret admirer in Mademoiselle Virginie, who, in spite of her dower of fifty thousand crowns, had as yet no suitor. Nothing could be more natural than these two passions at cross-purposes, born in the silence of the dingy shop, as violets bloom in the depths of a wood. The mute and constant looks which made the young people’s eyes meet by sheer need of change in the midst of persistent work and cloistered peace, was sure, sooner or later, to give rise to feelings of love.

这样，她们那与父亲的身份看似十分相称的乐趣，便常常被家庭习惯与家规中的种种情形弄得寡淡无味。
至于她们的日常生活，一句话便可画尽。纪尧姆太太要求女儿们清早便穿戴整齐，每天同一钟点下楼，并以修道院般的规律安排她们的活计。然而奥古斯丁碰巧得天独厚，生就一颗足以感到这种生活之空虚的高贵心灵。她那双蓝眼睛有时会抬起来，仿佛要穿透那阴暗的楼梯和那些潮湿库房的深处。在探过那修道院似的深沉寂静之后，她似乎在聆听激情之生命的遥远的、模糊的启示——那是一种把情感看得比事物贵重的生命。每逢这样的时刻，她的面颊会泛起红晕，闲着的双手把细纱针线活搁在光滑的橡木柜台上，母亲随即会开口，连最温柔的声调里也带着酸味：「奥古斯丁，我的宝贝，你在想什么？」奥古斯丁在纪尧姆太太新近辞退的一个厨娘的柜子里翻出过两部小说——《伊波利特·德·格拉斯伯爵》和《德·科曼热伯爵》——过去那个冬天漫长的夜里，她偷偷把它们吞咽下肚；这两部书或许促成了这位少女思想的发展。
就这样，奥古斯丁那怅惘的神情、温柔的声音、茉莉般的皮肤和蓝眼睛，在可怜的勒巴灵魂里点燃了一团火，炽热而又虔敬。出于一种不难理解的任性，奥古斯丁对这孤儿并无情意；她也许根本不知道他爱她。反过来，这位大伙计——长腿、栗色头发、大手大脚、身板结实——却在维尔日妮小姐那里得到了一位隐秘的仰慕者；她虽有五万埃居的陪嫁，至今尚无求婚者。这两段阴差阳错的爱情再自然不过了：它们诞生在昏暗店铺的静默里，如同紫罗兰开在密林深处。在持久的劳作与修道院式的安宁之中，年轻人纯粹出于调剂的默契对视，迟早要生出爱情的情感来。

The habit of seeing always the same face leads insensibly to our reading there the qualities of the soul, and at last effaces all its defects.

From that day the old merchant, grieved at seeing his eldest daughter fade, remembered how he had married Mademoiselle Chevrel under much the same circumstances as those of Joseph Lebas and Virginie. A good bit of business, to marry off his daughter, and discharge a sacred debt by repaying to an orphan the benefit he had formerly received from his predecessor under similar conditions! Joseph Lebas, who was now three-and-thirty, was aware of the obstacle which a difference of fifteen years placed between Augustine and himself. So the hapless assistant, whose heart was as warm as his legs were long and his chest deep, suffered in silence.
This was the state of the affairs in the tiny republic which, in the heart of the Rue Saint-Denis, was not unlike a dependency of La Trappe. But to give a full account of events as well as of feelings, it is needful to go back to some months before the scene with which this story opens. At dusk one evening, a young man passing the darkened shop of the Cat and Racket, had paused for a moment to gaze at a picture which might have arrested every painter in the world. The shop was not yet lighted, and was as a dark cave beyond which the dining-room was visible. A hanging lamp shed the yellow light which lends such charm to pictures of the Dutch school. The white linen, the silver, the cut glass, were brilliant accessories, and made more picturesque by strong contrasts of light and shade.

从那天起，老商人眼见长女日渐憔悴，心里难过，想起自己当年娶谢弗勒尔小姐，境况正与今日约瑟夫·勒巴和维尔日妮相仿。把女儿嫁出去，同时把先辈在同样情形下施与自己的恩惠偿还给一个孤儿，了却一桩神圣的债务——这可是一笔好买卖！约瑟夫·勒巴如今三十三岁，明白十五岁之差横在他与奥古斯丁之间是一道障碍。他又太有眼力，不会看不透纪尧姆先生的用意；他深知老人家不可动摇的原则：次女绝不先于长女出嫁。于是这个不幸的伙计——心和他的长腿、他的深胸腔一样热——只有默默忍受。
这就是圣但尼街中心那个小小共和国内的情势；说它是拉特拉普修道院的一个分院也不为过。但要把事情和感情都交代完整，就得回到本书开场那一幕之前几个月去。一天傍晚，暮色四合，一个年轻人路过尚未点灯的猫打球商店，停下来凝望了一阵一幅足以叫世上任何画家驻足的图画。店铺还没有上灯，黑黢黢的如同一个洞穴，洞穴后面却望得见饭厅。一盏吊灯洒下黄色的光，正是那种给荷兰画派的画作平添魅力的光。白台布、银器、雕花玻璃，都是亮眼的点缀，在强烈的光影对照中更显出画意。
